subject: Pay structure matrix: guidance, geo multipliers, and benchmarking notes
messages:
From: Karthik Iyer <karthik@redwood.com>
To: Neha Kapoor <neha@redwood.com>, Laura Bennett <laura@redwood.com>, Vivek Kulkarni <vivek@redwood.com>, Marcus Lin <marcus@redwood.com>
Date: Mon, 18 May 2026 09:12:00 -0700
Subject: Pay structure matrix: guidance, geo multipliers, and benchmarking notes

Team —

I pulled together a first pass of the pay-structure matrix (attached) to address a few recurring asks from hiring managers: clearer leveling definitions, explicit geo multipliers, and a lightweight benchmarking note for external vendor context. This is intended to be an operational guide for offers through Q3 and for headcount planning conversations.

High level: 
- Leveling: I added short behavior anchors for each band (IC3–IC7) so hiring managers have language to justify placement during offer review.
- Geo bands: proposing a default multiplier table (us-west = 1.00, us-east = 1.03, eu = 0.88, apac = 0.72). These are intentionally conservative; they align to Mercer regional medians in the attached summary.
- Benchmarks: Mercer summary attached (vendor note). We used a hybrid approach: medians for like-role SaaS comp, blended with our historical hire outcomes.

Asks: 
1) Neha — confirm the packet language we use in offers for remote hires (should we call them "location-adjusted base" or "market-adjusted base"?).
2) Laura — can you flag any lines in the matrix that will materially change open offer approvals for your recruiters? I want to surface exceptions ahead of Friday's recruiting sync.
3) Vivek/Marcus — any concerns on budget impact for FY26 Q3? I included an example scenario tab in the sheet showing ~+8% net spend if we fully equalize to US medians.

Attachment: 2026-05-18_pay-matrix-draft.xlsx (matrix + scenario tab).

Thanks —
Karthik
Karthik Iyer
Head of Talent Operations (interim)
Redwood Inference

From: Neha Kapoor <neha@redwood.com>
To: Karthik Iyer <karthik@redwood.com>, Laura Bennett <laura@redwood.com>, Vivek Kulkarni <vivek@redwood.com>, Marcus Lin <marcus@redwood.com>
Cc: Morgan Stern <m.mstern@mercersvc.com>
Date: Mon, 18 May 2026 11:07:00 -0700
Subject: Re: Pay structure matrix: guidance, geo multipliers, and benchmarking notes

Thanks Karthik — useful start. Quick notes inline and a couple of suggestions: 

- Language: prefer "market-adjusted base" — clearer for recruiting and avoids implying an individual-level negotiation.
- Remote hires: add a short clause that total target comp (base + target bonus) may be normalized to the market band for the hire location for equity calculations.
- Geo multipliers: fine as a starting point. One practical ask — can we add a footnote for "exception queue" where hiring managers can request discretionary uplift for critical hires (requires GR approval)? We need an explicit workflow to avoid ad hoc approvals via Slack.

Morgan (CC'd) — could you confirm Mercer sample size for APAC medians you shared? The summary shows small n in Singapore; curious whether we should upweight regional SEA markets differently.

Neha
Head of People Ops
Redwood Inference

From: Morgan Stern <m.mstern@mercersvc.com>
To: Neha Kapoor <neha@redwood.com>, Karthik Iyer <karthik@redwood.com>, Laura Bennett <laura@redwood.com>, Vivek Kulkarni <vivek@redwood.com>
Date: Mon, 18 May 2026 17:30:00 +0100
Subject: Re: Pay structure matrix: guidance, geo multipliers, and benchmarking notes

Neha —

Thanks for the ping. Quick clarifications on Mercer inputs: 
- APAC medians: Singapore sample n is small for some specialty infra roles (n<20). We recommend treating APAC composite as cautious — use +/−5% tolerance for early Q3.
- EU: we set medians using London/Frankfurt blend which matches the main hubs you hire into.
- Methodology: the attached PDF outlines our approach; we calculate regional multipliers off the US national median for like-role SaaS engineering functions.

I've attached the PDF summary (mercers-benchmark-summary-2026.pdf). If you'd like, we can run a bespoke request for the infra/serving-engineer job family next week (turnaround ~5 business days).

—Morgan
Morgan Stern
Senior Consultant, Compensation Insights
Mercer Services

From: Laura Bennett <laura@redwood.com>
To: Karthik Iyer <karthik@redwood.com>, Neha Kapoor <neha@redwood.com>, Vivek Kulkarni <vivek@redwood.com>, Marcus Lin <marcus@redwood.com>
Date: Wed, 20 May 2026 06:45:00 -0700
Subject: Re: Pay structure matrix: guidance, geo multipliers, and benchmarking notes

All — quick operational check after reviewing the matrix and Mercer's note. Recruiters called out two bands where offers will likely need manual review (IC5 senior engineering and IC6 staff engineering in EU region) because our current pipeline is priced slightly above the proposed EU multipliers.

Proposal: for open reqs created before June 1, let current offer practice stand (we'll honor existing pricing). For new reqs after June 1, apply the market-adjusted base and route exceptions to the "exception queue" (Neha to define approvals). That will buy us time to reforecast spend into the Q3 capex plan without disrupting active candidates.

I'm okay with the proposed language and the matrix otherwise. If no objections by COB Friday I'll mark this as policy guidance and ask Karthik to roll the sheet into the HR drive and update the offer templates.

Best,
Laura Bennett
VP, Talent Acquisition
Redwood Inference
